title: Fylgja twin record 1
description: One named twin in the state store, the same on every runtime, and the twin resource the API serves: what a client asked for (spec) and what the reconcile loop last saw (status), as Kubernetes shapes a resource, without Kubernetes (D-025).
$comment: STORE. The local store keeps each record in its own file (twins/<name>.json), the object store under the same key. ONE REPRESENTATION. The API's GET /v1/twins/{name} answers this document as it is stored; clients write spec alone (PUT), never status. COMPARE-AND-SET. Every write names the revision it read and fails if the stored revision differs (412 at the API with problem rule twin.conflict, a retry inside the loop); a successful write stores revision + 1, and the API serves the revision as the ETag. A new record is written with revision 1 only where no record exists. GENERATIONS. generation increases by one on every change to spec and when deletion is requested; the loop copies it to status.observed_generation once it has acted on it, so a client sees whether status is current: the twin is what was asked for when the two are equal and the Ready condition is True. RESUMPTION. status.phase is written before the next phase begins (Constitution VIII), so a restarted core resumes from it; status.run_id names the run whose events the loop is appending. A record with deletion_requested_at set is torn down by the loop and then deleted; a restarted core resumes the teardown.

record_version.description: The format's version; the store's reader refuses any other.

name.description: The twin's name and store key; the API path, the driver's isolation unit and every resource label carry it.

revision.description: The record's write counter; every writer's compare-and-set compares it.

generation.description: Incremented by one on every change to spec and on a deletion request; the loop compares it with status.observed_generation, and a watch reports it.

deletion_requested_at.description: When a client asked for the twin's deletion (DELETE); the loop tears it down and then deletes the record. Absent otherwise.

blueprint_id.description: The blueprint to run, when the client named one; the loop compiles it to a bundle.

bundle_id.description: The bundle to run, when the client named one directly; the loop plans it with no compile.

driver.description: The driver the twin runs on, fixed at creation (the server's default when the client named none); a PUT naming another is refused (twin.driver.fixed). The loop calls only it.

allow_restart.description: Whether the loop may restart or recreate nodes to reach this spec; a change that needs a restart without it is refused before anything is touched (rule step.restart.refused).

spec.description: What the twin should be: written by a client's PUT, by compare-and-set, never by the loop. Changing it steps the twin (D-025).

observed_generation.description: The generation the loop last acted on; 0 before it first has. With the Ready condition, it tells a client the twin is what spec asks for.

conditions.description: Ready, Stepping and Diverged, each at most once; show, list and the orchestrator branch on them.

phase.description: The last phase the loop completed toward the current generation; a restarted core resumes after it.

run_id.description: The run the loop is executing for the current generation; absent when idle. The loop appends events to it after a restart.

blueprint_id.description: The blueprint of the bundle the twin runs; show and the orchestrator read it.

bundle_id.description: The bundle the twin runs; verify reads its expectations from it, a step diffs from it.

deployment_id.description: The driver's plan applied; a step compares the new plan with it, show reports its fidelity.

nodes.description: Every runtime node the twin holds, probe hosts included, sorted by name; the push, readiness, verify and flows reach nodes through it.

last_step.description: The latest step's outcome; show and the orchestrator's report read it.

status.description: What the reconcile loop last saw: written only by the loop, by compare-and-set; clients read and watch it.

twin_name.description: A DNS-1123 label of at most 40 characters, so a driver can name a lab or a namespace after it with a prefix.

run_id.description: A run's id, a ULID, so runs sort by start.

type.description: Ready: every node holds the bundle and answers. Stepping: a step is in flight. Diverged: a step failed after touching the twin and nothing was torn down. Clients branch on it.

status.description: Whether the condition holds; clients branch on it.

reason.description: The stable rule id that set it (e.g. readiness.timeout); a client looks up its wording.

since.description: When status last changed; clients show how long a condition has held.

name.description: The bundle's node name, or a probe host's <probe>-a/-b; joins the record to the manifest.

handle.description: The driver's own handle for the node (container name, namespace/pod, device id); the driver's inspect, exec and destroy use it.

address.description: The node's management address from the driver's endpoints(); the push, readiness, verify and flows dial it. Absent until known.

access.description: The host through which a client outside the runtime reaches address; absent when address is directly reachable. On clabernetes each node's LoadBalancer IP is its address, so it is absent there (D-020); a bastion or ingress, should one return, would set it. The thin CLI and the orchestrator read it.

holds.description: The bundle whose config the node was last pushed; verify asserts it equals bundle_id, the step's push decides from it. Absent for a probe host and before the first push. Valid only for the recorded incarnation.

incarnation.description: The driver's identity of the node's current instance: the container's StartedAt locally, the pod uid on clabernetes. A step or a runtime event can replace a node and lose its push (locally, cEOS restarted on a link change; on clabernetes, pods replaced on restart, recreate and any change to the node's spec; verified on containerlab 0.79 and clabernetes 0.10.1, 2026-10-30), so the loop treats holds as void whenever inspect reports a different incarnation, and re-pushes.

outcome.description: How the step ended, or running; show and the orchestrator read it.

from.description: The bundle stepped from; show and the report read it.

to.description: The bundle stepped to; show and the report read it.

phase.description: The last phase the step completed; a diverged step's report names where it stopped.

run_id.description: The step's run; its verdict (findings, wait and loss) and events are read through it, so they are not copied here.
